subject: economics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A competition authority is most likely to block or scrutinise a merger that would:
options: increase the number of competing firms
substantially lessen competition and raise prices for consumers
reduce a firm's costs through economies of scale
create a small new entrant
questions.explain: Mergers are challenged chiefly where they would substantially lessen competition and harm consumers through higher prices or less choice.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-tariff barrier to trade?
options: A floating exchange rate
Strict domestic technical and safety standards applied to imports
An ad valorem import duty
A specific per-unit tax on imports
questions.explain: Non-tariff barriers include regulations, standards and administrative rules that restrict imports without using a formal tariff.

questions.q: Absolute advantage exists when a country can produce a good using:
options: fewer resources (more output per input) than another country
a fixed exchange rate
a higher tariff than another country
a lower opportunity cost than another country
questions.explain: Absolute advantage is about greater productive efficiency (more output per unit of input), distinct from comparative advantage's opportunity-cost basis.

questions.q: In the UK balance of payments, the current account does NOT include the:
options: purchase of foreign equities by UK residents
trade in services balance
primary income (investment income) balance
trade in goods balance
questions.explain: Purchases of foreign equities are financial-account transactions; the current account covers trade, primary income and secondary income.

questions.q: 'Speculative bubbles' in asset markets are an example of market failure in finance because:
options: they are caused solely by central-bank policy
they only ever benefit consumers
prices always equal fundamental value
herding and mispriced risk drive prices far from fundamentals, with costly crashes
questions.explain: Bubbles reflect herd behaviour and mispriced risk, pushing asset prices away from fundamentals and imposing wider costs when they burst.

questions.q: The Human Development Index (HDI) combines life expectancy, education and:
options: the Gini coefficient
the current-account balance
the unemployment rate
gross national income per capita (PPP)
questions.explain: HDI is a composite of life expectancy at birth, mean/expected years of schooling and GNI per head at PPP.

questions.q: The principal-agent problem in a large public company arises because:
options: there is no separation of ownership and control
all firms maximise profit perfectly
managers always act in shareholders' interests
shareholders (principals) and managers (agents) may have divergent objectives
questions.explain: Separation of ownership (principals/shareholders) from control (agents/managers) can lead managers to pursue their own goals.

questions.q: Ring-fencing retail banking from investment banking (e.g. under post-2008 reforms) is designed to:
options: protect everyday deposits and payments from losses in riskier investment activities
abolish commercial banking
remove all financial regulation
increase the risk to ordinary depositors
questions.explain: Ring-fencing separates core retail services from speculative investment activities so that depositors are insulated from trading losses.

questions.q: Under a freely floating exchange-rate system, the external value of a currency is determined by:
options: the rate set by the IMF
the central bank's official target
the level of foreign-exchange reserves held
the supply of and demand for the currency on the foreign-exchange market
questions.explain: In a clean float the rate is set purely by market supply and demand, with no official intervention.

questions.q: A current-account deficit on the balance of payments means that, broadly:
options: exports of goods and services exceed imports
imports of goods and services (plus net income/transfers) exceed exports
the financial account is in deficit
the government budget is in deficit
questions.explain: A current-account deficit arises when outflows for imports, income and transfers exceed the corresponding inflows from exports.

questions.q: The Marshall-Lerner condition states that a currency depreciation will improve the trade balance only if the:
options: sum of the price elasticities of demand for exports and imports exceeds one
exchange rate is fixed by the central bank
income elasticity of imports is less than one
capital account is in surplus
questions.explain: Marshall-Lerner: depreciation improves the current account when the combined (absolute) price elasticities of export and import demand are greater than unity.

questions.q: The risk that a bank cannot meet immediate demands for cash even though it is solvent is known as:
options: market risk
credit risk
systemic surplus
liquidity risk
questions.explain: Liquidity risk is the danger of being unable to meet short-term cash demands despite holding assets exceeding liabilities.

questions.q: Export-led growth as a development strategy typically relies on:
options: reducing the savings ratio
raising import tariffs to protect all home industries
fixing prices below market levels
exploiting comparative advantage to expand output sold abroad
questions.explain: Export-led (outward-looking) growth uses trade and comparative advantage to widen markets and raise productivity.

questions.q: A principal role of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) is to:
options: oversee multilateral trade agreements and adjudicate trade disputes
set the value of members' exchange rates
fix world commodity prices
provide development loans to low-income countries
questions.explain: The WTO administers trade rules, promotes liberalisation and resolves disputes between members; lending and exchange rates fall to other bodies.

questions.q: The J-curve effect describes how, following a currency depreciation, the trade balance:
options: remains constant throughout
worsens at first before improving as quantities adjust
improves immediately and then worsens
moves only if the exchange rate is fixed
questions.explain: In the short run demand is inelastic so the trade balance worsens; as volumes respond over time it improves, tracing a J shape.

questions.q: An investment bank's typical activities include:
options: advising on mergers and underwriting securities issues
running the country's monetary policy
printing legal-tender banknotes
accepting retail savings accounts only
questions.explain: Investment banks specialise in capital-market services such as underwriting, advisory work, and trading, rather than retail deposit-taking.

questions.q: A central bank acting as 'lender of last resort' will:
options: guarantee that every bank will always make a profit
set the price of every share on the stock market
take ownership of all commercial banks
provide liquidity to solvent banks facing a temporary shortage of funds
questions.explain: As lender of last resort the central bank supplies emergency liquidity to fundamentally solvent banks to prevent contagion.

questions.q: A key limitation of using GDP per capita alone to measure development is that it:
options: always overstates inflation
cannot be measured at purchasing-power parity
excludes government spending
ignores distribution, non-marketed output and quality-of-life factors
questions.explain: GDP per head says nothing about income distribution, informal activity, health, education or environmental quality.

questions.q: A tariff imposed by a small importing country on a good will most directly cause:
options: an increase in domestic consumer surplus
a rise in domestic production and a fall in imports
a reduction in government revenue
a fall in the domestic price of the good
questions.explain: A tariff raises the domestic price, encouraging domestic supply and reducing imports while generating tariff revenue.

questions.q: The primary remit of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is to:
options: set tariffs for member states
finance long-term infrastructure projects
provide concessional loans only to the poorest countries
promote global monetary cooperation and provide short-term balance-of-payments support
questions.explain: The IMF oversees the monetary system and lends to members facing balance-of-payments problems, often with conditionality.

questions.q: Which is a reason some firms deliberately remain small?
options: They always face rising average costs at low output
Economies of scale are available at every output
Small firms cannot survive in any market
Niche markets, owner control, and limited demand make expansion unattractive
questions.explain: Niche or local markets, the desire for personal control, and limited total demand can make staying small rational.

questions.q: Which of the following is most likely to cause a deterioration in a developing primary-exporter's terms of trade over the long run?
options: A persistent rise in world commodity prices
Low income elasticity of demand for primary products relative to manufactures
Membership of a customs union
An appreciation of its currency
questions.explain: The Prebisch-Singer hypothesis links low income elasticity for primaries (and high elasticity for manufactures) to a secular decline in primary exporters' terms of trade.

questions.q: Globalisation has been driven by all of the following EXCEPT:
options: rising worldwide tariff barriers
containerisation and improved logistics
trade liberalisation and the growth of multinationals
falling transport and communication costs
questions.explain: Globalisation has been propelled by falling barriers, cheaper transport/communication and MNCs; rising tariffs work against it.

questions.q: Forcing a monopoly to set price equal to marginal cost (allocative efficiency) can be problematic because, for a natural monopoly, it may:
options: result in the firm making a loss where MC is below average cost
raise price above the monopoly level
eliminate all consumer surplus
always generate supernormal profit
questions.explain: For a natural monopoly with falling average cost, MC lies below AC, so marginal-cost pricing yields a loss requiring subsidy.

questions.q: 'Sales (volume) maximisation' as a firm objective typically means producing where:
options: output is the largest consistent with at least normal profit (AR = AC)
marginal revenue is positive
marginal cost exceeds marginal revenue greatly
average revenue is maximised
questions.explain: Sales maximisation seeks the highest output subject to a normal-profit constraint, i.e. where average revenue covers average cost.

questions.q: A stock (equity) market primarily allows companies to:
options: raise long-term finance by issuing shares to investors
borrow short-term funds from the central bank
insure against exchange-rate risk only
set their own corporation-tax rate
questions.explain: Equity markets enable firms to raise long-term capital by selling ownership shares and provide secondary-market liquidity.

questions.q: Two firms at the same stage of production in the same industry merging is called:
options: vertical integration
diversification
horizontal integration
conglomerate integration
questions.explain: Horizontal integration combines firms at the same stage of the same industry, often to gain market share and scale.

questions.q: Internal economies of scale are reductions in long-run average cost that arise from:
options: government subsidies
the growth of the individual firm itself
the growth of the whole industry
a fall in market demand
questions.explain: Internal economies of scale stem from the firm's own expansion (e.g. technical, purchasing, managerial), lowering its LRAC.

questions.q: Country X can produce both wheat and cloth using fewer resources than Country Y. According to comparative advantage, mutually beneficial trade is still possible provided:
options: both countries fix their exchange rates
Country Y subsidises its exports
the opportunity-cost ratios of the two goods differ between the countries
Country X has a balance-of-payments surplus
questions.explain: Gains from trade arise whenever opportunity-cost (and hence relative-cost) ratios differ, even if one country has absolute advantage in both goods.

questions.q: Trade diversion occurs when the formation of a trading bloc causes a country to switch its imports from a:
options: higher-cost member to a lower-cost external producer
lower-cost external producer to a higher-cost member producer
domestic firm to a foreign firm
monopolist to a competitive supplier
questions.explain: Trade diversion is the welfare-reducing shift away from an efficient non-member toward a less efficient member because the latter avoids the external tariff.
